voiceover: Nabeel Qureshi was a devout Ahmadi Muslim, a gifted defender of Islam, and a student headed for a career in medicine. At university he befriended a Christian, David Wood, and the two began years of respectful dialogue — the reliability of the Gospels, the evidence around Jesus' death and resurrection, the textual history of the Qur'an. He loved Islam. He did not want the conversation to go where it was going, and he resisted the conclusion. Following Jesus, he knew, would cost him nearly everything: his family, and the community that had raised him. But after years of study, prayer, and dreams he could not dismiss, he came to faith in Christ in 2005. He told the story in 'Seeking Allah, Finding Jesus' — a New York Times bestseller. He earned his MD, then gave his life to apologetics, speaking at Oxford, Cambridge, and more than a hundred universities for the faith he had once resisted. He died of cancer in 2017, at just thirty-four. Faithful to the end. He followed the evidence — whatever it cost.
